# Yarilo

> Yarilo is a cloud-native mail server written in Go: IMAP, POP3, LMTP,
> Submission, JMAP and Sieve, designed for Kubernetes.

Full documentation as a single file: https://doc.yarilomail.org/main/llms-full.txt

## Documentation

- [Backend HTTP API](https://doc.yarilomail.org/main/architecture/backend_api.html): yarilo-backend-api exposes the operator surface for per-account state over HTTP: dict, ACL, quota, folders, users, index, mdbox storage, messages, subscriptions, special-use, metadata, sessions and full-text search. One instance runs per backend pod in the co-located layout, or as its own Deployment otherwise.
- [Director configuration](https://doc.yarilomail.org/main/architecture/director.html): yarilo-director keeps the routing state of a cluster: which backend serves each user. Login pods ask it with a LOOKUP before they open a session to a backend.
- [yarilo-director HTTP admin API](https://doc.yarilomail.org/main/architecture/director_api.html): Director-plane admin endpoints exposed by yarilo-director on port 9103 (default). The API speaks plain HTTP. Every endpoint requires a Bearer token; an IP allow-list can be added on top.
- [Architecture](https://doc.yarilomail.org/main/architecture/): This document is the authoritative reference for yarilo's architecture. All development decisions must be consistent with what is written here. If something in the code contradicts this document — the code is wrong.
- [Feature coverage](https://doc.yarilomail.org/main/architecture/parity.html): What yarilo implements, feature by feature, so that planning a migration is a matter of reading a list rather than of trying things out.
- [Services configuration](https://doc.yarilomail.org/main/architecture/services.html): The services section controls which listeners are started and how each one behaves at the network level. Each service is a named block under services:. A missing key or enabled: false means the listener is not started.
- [Authentication configuration](https://doc.yarilomail.org/main/auth/): Yarilo authenticates IMAP/POP3/Submission credentials against an ordered chain of passdb entries. The first passdb that returns a definitive result (success or failure for a known user) wins. Unknown users fall through to the next entry. A temporary failure — a database that does not answer — stops the chain there: the login is answered as a temporary failure, not passed to the next entry.
- [Master users](https://doc.yarilomail.org/main/auth/master_users.html): A master user is an administrative identity allowed to log into another user's mailbox with its own password — the target's password is never involved. Typical uses: mailbox migrations, support access, automated per-user maintenance.
- [OAuth 2.0 / OAUTHBEARER + XOAUTH2 Integration](https://doc.yarilomail.org/main/auth/oauth2.html): yarilo-auth validates OAuth 2.0 bearer tokens for the SASL OAUTHBEARER (RFC 7628) and XOAUTH2 (Google/Microsoft legacy extension) mechanisms and exposes them as a passdb so OAuth logins flow through the same chain machinery as SQL logins (cache, penalty, policy, audit log — all work unchanged).
- [Auth Penalty (cross-pod IP backoff)](https://doc.yarilomail.org/main/auth/penalty.html): yarilo-auth can enforce a per-client-IP exponential backoff on failed auth attempts. The counter lives in the yarilo-warden service so a single attacker IP pays the cost across every auth pod they land on — pod load-balancing does not let them reset by landing on a fresh pod.
- [Auth Policy Server Integration](https://doc.yarilomail.org/main/auth/policy.html): yarilo-auth can POST every login attempt to an external HTTP policy service that decides whether to allow, reject, or tarpit the request. The wire shape follows the wforce (weakforced) HTTP API so any policy server speaking that dialect plugs in without a custom adapter.
- [SCRAM family (SHA-256 and SHA-1, each with optional PLUS)](https://doc.yarilomail.org/main/auth/scram.html): yarilo-auth supports the Salted Challenge Response Authentication Mechanism family (RFC 5802 / RFC 7677) as a SASL mechanism in IMAP, POP3 and Submission. SCRAM is the recommended replacement for plain-text + TLS auth: the server never sees the user's password, and the client proves possession through a salted HMAC ladder that resists offline brute-force on the wire.
- [wforce Integration](https://doc.yarilomail.org/main/auth/wforce.html): weakforced (wforce) is a policy server that counts login failures and answers whether a login may go on. This page deploys it next to yarilo on Kubernetes with a policy against password guessing, connects yarilo-auth to it and turns it on in stages.
- [Full-text search](https://doc.yarilomail.org/main/features/fts.html): Full-text search answers IMAP SEARCH BODY, SEARCH TEXT and SEARCH HEADER, and JMAP Email/query text filters, from a per-user index instead of reading every message.
- [Sieve Mail Filtering](https://doc.yarilomail.org/main/features/sieve.html): Yarilo implements server-side mail filtering via the Sieve language (RFC 5228). Scripts are stored per-user and executed on every incoming LMTP delivery. Script management is available via the ManageSieve protocol (RFC 5804) on port 4190.
- [Virtual Mailboxes](https://doc.yarilomail.org/main/features/virtual.html): A virtual mailbox holds no messages of its own. It shows messages that live in other folders of the same user, chosen by a rule: all mail in INBOX and the archive, every unread message, every flagged one. Reading, flagging, searching and expunging in a virtual mailbox act on the real message in its folder.
- [Yarilo Documentation](https://doc.yarilomail.org/main/): Yarilo is a mail server written in Go and built for Kubernetes. It serves IMAP, POP3, LMTP, Submission, JMAP and ManageSieve, filters mail with Sieve, and stores it in maildir, sdbox or mdbox.
- [Deployment](https://doc.yarilomail.org/main/installation/deployment.html): Deployment topology, sizing, and high availability. This is a design-level reference; for step-by-step setup see the Installation Guide.
- [DNS records for a mail domain: MX, SPF, DKIM, DMARC and PTR](https://doc.yarilomail.org/main/installation/dns.html): The DNS records a mail domain needs before yarilo can receive and send mail reliably, and why the nameservers serving them need redundancy of their own. For the cluster-side setup see the Installation Guide.
- [Running yarilo with Docker Compose](https://doc.yarilomail.org/main/installation/docker_compose.html): A single-host standalone deployment for local development, evaluation and small self-hosted installs. It mirrors the standalone topology from the Helm chart, on one host, with Docker Compose.
- [General configuration](https://doc.yarilomail.org/main/installation/general.html): The general section defines infrastructure settings shared across all listeners. Individual services can override ssl per-listener with their own ssl: block.
- [Installation Guide](https://doc.yarilomail.org/main/installation/): Yarilo installs two ways. Pick the one that matches your target:
- [Migration and backfill](https://doc.yarilomail.org/main/installation/migration.html): yarilo-migrate is the operator tool for bringing an existing mail store under yarilo, and for filling in per-message state that newer features need. It has three modes, and they answer three different questions.
- [Security policy](https://doc.yarilomail.org/main/operations/security.html): Do not report security issues in public issues, pull requests or discussions. Report them privately, so the issue can be fixed before it is disclosed.
- [End-to-end smoke test](https://doc.yarilomail.org/main/operations/smoke.html): Drives a live yarilo instance through the full happy-path mail flow: authenticate → deliver → read.
- [Testing](https://doc.yarilomail.org/main/operations/testing.html): There are two smoke binaries, and which one to reach for depends on the question. They are not alternatives.
- [yarctl](https://doc.yarilomail.org/main/operations/yarilo_admin.html): Unified operator CLI for yarilo. Three top-level planes:
- [IMAP configuration](https://doc.yarilomail.org/main/protocols/imap.html): Yarilo implements IMAP4rev2 (RFC 9051) with backward compatibility to IMAP4rev1 (RFC 3501).
- [JMAP configuration](https://doc.yarilomail.org/main/protocols/jmap.html): The session resource, the request envelope and the Mail and Quota methods listed under Capabilities are served, reading and writing. Push is served over EventSource (Push); WebSocket and Web Push are not yet.
- [LMTP configuration](https://doc.yarilomail.org/main/protocols/lmtp.html): LMTP (RFC 2033) is the Local Mail Transfer Protocol used for final delivery from an external MTA (Postfix, Exim, etc.) into the yarilo mailbox. It operates on port 24 and returns per-recipient status codes, making it a drop-in replacement for SMTP-based local delivery.
- [POP3 configuration](https://doc.yarilomail.org/main/protocols/pop3.html): Yarilo implements POP3 (RFC 1939) with STLS (RFC 2595), UIDL, CAPA, and XCLIENT.
- [Submission configuration](https://doc.yarilomail.org/main/protocols/submission.html): Yarilo runs two submission listeners. MX inbound (port 25) is handled by an external MTA (Postfix, Exim, etc.) which delivers to yarilo via LMTP (port 24).
- [RFC support](https://doc.yarilomail.org/main/reference/rfcs.html): The standards each yarilo service implements, and how far. A row is yes only when the code serves it and, for an extension a client discovers, the server advertises it: a command a client is never told about is, to that client, absent.
- [All settings](https://doc.yarilomail.org/main/reference/settings.html): Every documented yarilo.yaml setting, grouped by section. Each name links to its full description, and the type and default are repeated here for a quick scan.
- [Dictionaries](https://doc.yarilomail.org/main/storage/dict.html): pkg/dict is the general key-value store every yarilo feature that needs durable per-user or per-mailbox state sits on top of. A single contract (Dict + Tx + Iterator) is satisfied by multiple drivers; the choice of driver (file, redis, sql, memory, fail) is made via YAML config, not code. The drivers run in the yarilo-dict service (mTLS, port 9107); a session binary names a dict and reaches it through pkg/dict/proxy, and needs dict_service.dict_addr set to start — see The dict service.
- [Mailbox storage](https://doc.yarilomail.org/main/storage/): Mailbox backends (Maildir, sdbox, mdbox) and the FileIndex (binary mail-index v7.3 wire format: .index / .index.log / .index.names). All index mutations go through the cross-process mailbox lock (yarilo-locks); sessions sharing a pod serialise on an in-process sync.RWMutex — the Redis lock is only ever contested across pods, not within a single pod. See also mdbox Alt Storage (Cold Tiering).
- [mdbox Alt Storage (Cold Tiering)](https://doc.yarilomail.org/main/storage/mdbox_alt.html): yarilo mdbox supports moving messages to a secondary (cold) storage tier — functionally equivalent to the reference's alt-path setting and its alt-move command. Messages moved to alt storage remain fully accessible; the Fetch path transparently falls back to the alt directory when a file is not found in primary.
- [Namespaces](https://doc.yarilomail.org/main/storage/namespace.html): yarilo supports the three RFC 9051 namespace classes:
- [Other users' mailboxes](https://doc.yarilomail.org/main/storage/owner_shared_ns.html): A user can open another user's mailboxes under a namespace such as user/alice/, when alice's ACL allows it. The namespace is configured once, and yarilo resolves each owner's storage the first time a session names that owner.
- [Quota (RFC 9208)](https://doc.yarilomail.org/main/storage/quota.html): yarilo implements per-user storage and message-count quota via the IMAP QUOTA extension (RFC 9208) and the pkg/quota package.
